how_measured: POST https://csjekrvukbdznetsrodj.supabase.co/auth/v1/admin/generate_link with the project's service_role key, type=recovery, email=test@more30.com (the single auth user on this project). generate_link builds the real link and returns it WITHOUT sending mail — no message left the system, per the test-mode rule.

before.reading: Two faults, not one. (a) site_url pointed at the recipient's own machine, so every reset/confirm/magic-link mail from this project led nowhere. (b) uri_allow_list was empty, so an app asking for its own path was refused too and silently fell back to the same localhost.

change.why_this_value: Identical to the two other reachable projects (uhnrgujbdxhhmoxcjria and bieebmnmkffwbqlsfozh, both https://more30.com). site_url is one value for the whole project and four systems sit on it at four different paths, so the root is the only honest default; the allow-list is what lets each of the four ask for its own path.

untouched.note: Both read back unchanged after the PATCH — the partial update did not disturb the signup fix from the previous step.

still_open: The link now lands on a page that exists, and that is all it does. Nothing in portal/ or in the four apps reads a PASSWORD_RECOVERY event or a #type=recovery fragment (searched portal/public, portal/src and the four app trees for PASSWORD_RECOVERY, type=recovery, resetPasswordForEmail, updateUser — no hits). A recipient who clicks now reaches more30.com with a live recovery token in the URL fragment and no screen that will spend it. Filed separately; this step deliberately did not build that screen.
